[LNUL.4.5] How a `where` predicate over a null slot `s.state: Float?` decides
whether the pattern matches:

| Predicate | Value when `s.state` is null | The pattern matches |
|---|---|---|
| `s.state > 85` | `null` | no |
| `not (s.state > 85)` | `null` | no |
| `(s.state ?? 0.0) > 85` | `false` | no: the author substituted `0.0` |
| `s.state is null` | `true` | yes |

A missing reading therefore fires neither a comparison nor its negation; a
null-as-false reading would fire the negation. `is null` is the only way to act
on absence ([LNUL.4.4]). `s.state == null` is a compile error: `==` propagates
null, so it could never be true.
